propositions: The complexity lock compares branch baseline against main tip instead of merge base, causing false violations when main lowers a ceiling and un-rebased branches still carry the pre-reduction baseline
Every future ceiling reduction on main will break all un-rebased branches identically by falsely reporting a raise, contradicting the shrink-only ratchet's purpose
The shallow fetch (--depth=1) of main is too shallow to compute a merge base; the fetch depth and checkout depth must be increased to support merge-base comparison

Branch complexity should be judged only against entries the branch itself changed, not against main-tip reductions, preserving fail-closed semantics by falling back to stricter tip comparison if merge base is unavailable
An un-rebased branch carrying pre-reduction baseline must pass the lock after main lowers a ceiling, verified against the merge-base commit's baseline
